articles.headline: El Celeiro se cubre de lenteja de agua en Sarria mientras el Ulla llega a Portodemouros sin caudal
articles.subtitle: La confederación atribuye la manta verde al bajo caudal del cauce y a las últimas lluvias, y descarta riesgos. En O Chanto sigue sin repararse la presa rota, y Ulloa Viva vincula la eutrofización del embalse a la captación prevista por Altri.
articles.body:
El río Celeiro aparece cubierto de un manto de lenteja de agua a su paso por Sarria, sobre todo junto a la estación de tren y en el barrio de As Insuas, mientras el cauce sufre su deterioro en el entorno del parque de O Chanto.

La Confederación Hidrográfica del Miño-Sil atribuye la proliferación a un «proceso natural»: el río lleva muy poco caudal y las últimas lluvias dejaron agua encharcada en la que se desarrolló la planta.

Técnicos del organismo tomaron muestras la semana pasada y sostienen que no supone «ningún riesgo». Los vecinos aseguran que la manta verde crece desde el verano y reclaman que se retire la basura acumulada, como una silla que lleva en el agua desde julio.

En O Chanto el problema es más antiguo: la presa está rota desde hace años y la autorización para repararla, solicitada por el titular de la concesión de agua, sigue en información pública desde mayo de 2025.

La terraza de un edificio municipal lleva apuntalada desde octubre de 2020 y de la playa fluvial creada hace seis décadas no queda nada. El pleno aprobó en julio una moción del PP para recuperar la zona, mientras el gobierno local dice que negocia con la confederación.

## El Ulla llega al embalse «casi sin agua»

La plataforma Ulloa Viva difundió a finales de septiembre imágenes del río Ulla a su llegada al embalse de Portodemouros, entre Santiso y Agolada, para denunciar la escasez de caudal y la eutrofización que, asegura, se repite cada año.

El colectivo lo relaciona con el proyecto de la celulosa de Altri en Palas de Rei, que prevé captar 46 millones de litros diarios durante 75 años y verter 60 toneladas de sulfatos al día. La Xunta declaró en septiembre el río en sequía prolongada.

articles.headline: El Lugo tumba al Logroñés y es líder en solitario tras cinco victorias seguidas
articles.subtitle: El equipo de Borja Fernández se impuso 3-1 en el Anxo Carro con un doblete de Chiqui, suma 19 de los últimos 21 puntos y es, junto al Barcelona, el único invicto de las tres primeras categorías del fútbol español.
articles.body:
El CD Lugo es líder en solitario de su grupo después de imponerse 3-1 a la UD Logroñés en el Anxo Carro, en el duelo entre los dos equipos que mejor habían arrancado la temporada. El conjunto de Borja Fernández acumula cinco victorias consecutivas y 19 de los últimos 21 puntos.

Chiqui firmó un doblete. Abrió el marcador al rematar en el segundo palo un centro de Arturo Palma y, antes de la media hora, cruzó un disparo junto al poste contrario después de conducir el balón desde la derecha. El árbitro había expulsado poco antes a Manu Pedre por derribar a Álex Costa cuando se marchaba solo hacia el área.

El Logroñés recortó distancias por medio de Anai Morales, que aprovechó el rechace de una falta antes del descanso. Ya en el tiempo añadido de la primera parte, Álex Costa vio la roja por empujar a un rival, y el Lugo afrontó la reanudación con diez.

Alan Godoy sentenció desde el punto de penalti, tras una internada de Palma en el área, para dejar el 3-1 definitivo y devolver la tranquilidad a la grada.

El triunfo deja al Lugo como el único equipo invicto de las tres primeras categorías españolas junto al Barcelona, un registro que el entrenador, Borja Fernández, quiso rebajar: «No creamos que somos los reyes del mambo simplemente porque ganamos algunos partidos».

articles.headline: San Froilán se despide con medio millar de drones y un Mercado Medieval en la Catedral
articles.subtitle: Las patronales de Lugo cerraron diez días de fiesta con un espectáculo aéreo sobre San Fiz en sustitución de los fuegos artificiales, tras una jornada de artesanía, oficios tradicionales y música en el atrio catedralicio.
articles.body:
El San Froilán cerró este lunes diez días de fiesta con el Mercado Medieval en el atrio de la Catedral y un espectáculo aéreo que sustituyó a los fuegos artificiales: medio millar de drones sobrevolaron San Fiz para despedir las patronales.

La jornada final combinó artesanía, música y oficios tradicionales, con talleres de caligrafía medieval, cuero o talla en madera, ajedrez en un tablero gigante, zancos y un tiovivo de madera para los más pequeños. Un dragón de cuatro metros de largo, O Dragón do Castelo, recorrió el atrio, donde también hubo malabares, circo y acrobacias.

Para los feriantes veteranos, la fiesta es una vida entera. Antonio Pereira, de 56 años, asa castañas en Lugo «desde que teño memoria», heredó el puesto de su padre y recuerda los distintos recintos feriales, desde los bajos del parque hasta la actual Horta do Seminario, que considera la mejor ubicación. El bingo que se instala a las puertas del Parque acumula treinta años y el tiovivo, medio siglo dando vueltas.

Los conciertos volvieron a llenar la Horta do Seminario, con Malú desbordando el recinto, y la hostelería de la ciudad cerró un puente con las habitaciones prácticamente agotadas.

articles.headline: El Supremo rechaza el recurso del Gobierno y deja sin voto el 29N a los nacionalizados por la 'ley de nietos'
articles.subtitle: La Sala de lo Contencioso ratifica la suspensión cautelar pedida por Vox e Iustitia Europa y veta inscribir en el censo exterior a quienes obtuvieron la nacionalidad de origen por esa vía, salvo los descendientes de exiliados que lo acrediten.
articles.body:
El Tribunal Supremo ha rechazado el recurso del Gobierno y mantiene la suspensión cautelar que impide votar el 29 de noviembre a las personas que obtuvieron la nacionalidad española de origen al amparo de la conocida como ley de nietos. La Sala de lo Contencioso-Administrativo ha dictado dos autos que desestiman las alegaciones de la Abogacía del Estado contra la medida adoptada en septiembre a petición de Vox e Iustitia Europa.

Los magistrados indican al Instituto Nacional de Estadística, del que depende la Oficina del Censo Electoral, que no puede inscribir en el Censo Electoral de Residentes Ausentes a quienes hayan obtenido esa nacionalidad y aún no figuren en él. Respecto a los que ya estaban inscritos, se mantiene la suspensión de sus efectos electorales en el proceso convocado por el real decreto de 5 de octubre.

La resolución abre una excepción: no regirá la suspensión para quienes los registros consulares certifiquen que, a 1 de agosto de 2026, tenían la condición de nacidos fuera de España, de padre, madre, abuelo o abuela originariamente españoles que hubieran sufrido exilio por razones políticas, ideológicas, de creencia o de orientación e identidad sexual y que hubieran perdido o renunciado a la nacionalidad.

El Supremo reitera que «el interés general de preservar la pureza del proceso electoral debe prevalecer sobre el derecho de sufragio» y recuerda que corresponde a la Administración revisar los expedientes. La decisión cierra además la puerta a un recurso del Ejecutivo ante el Tribunal Constitucional: solo los afectados podrán pedir amparo. Vox celebró el fallo y el PSOE lo rechazó acusando a PP y Vox de volver «a tropezar en la piedra del franquismo».

articles.headline: Los Reyes inician en Ceuta su primera visita a las ciudades autónomas en 19 años
articles.subtitle: Felipe VI y Letizia llegan este martes a Ceuta y Melilla tras la entrada masiva de migrantes de julio, con Marruecos advirtiendo del «chantaje» y Sánchez admitiendo que buques de guerra marroquíes entraron en aguas ceutíes.
articles.body:
Felipe VI y la reina Letizia inician este martes una visita histórica a Ceuta y Melilla, las dos ciudades autónomas cuya soberanía cuestiona Marruecos. No se producía un viaje de los monarcas a ambos enclaves desde noviembre de 2007, cuando Juan Carlos I y Sofía fueron recibidos por multitudes vestidas con los colores de la bandera.

El desplazamiento llega tres meses después de la entrada masiva de migrantes en Ceuta, un episodio que Pedro Sánchez calificó de «ataque» y «violación de la integridad territorial de España». El presidente admitió este lunes que buques de guerra marroquíes accedieron a aguas españolas coincidiendo con aquella llegada, aunque restó importancia: «Entre dos países vecinos ese tipo de hechos puntuales suceden».

Marruecos ha advertido del «chantaje» y de la instrumentalización de la visita, y mantiene un silencio oficial sobre el viaje. Rabat sostiene que las ciudades no son objeto de disputa en las conversaciones con España, mientras el Gobierno español evita entrar en el asunto de la soberanía, según las versiones publicadas por la prensa.

En Ceuta la crisis sigue sin resolverse del todo, con buena parte del vecindario pendiente de que se restablezca la normalidad. El líder de Vox, Santiago Abascal, ha aprovechado su presencia en la ciudad para exigir la «militarización» de la frontera y arremeter contra el «Gobierno de traidores», en una visita que se produce ya en plena precampaña de las generales del 29 de noviembre.

articles.headline: Vox se dispara a 68 escaños y supera al PP en Cataluña, según el sondeo de arranque de campaña
articles.subtitle: La encuesta de Sigma Dos para El Mundo mantiene la mayoría del bloque conservador en 203 diputados, con el PP en 135, el PSOE en 103 y Sumar hundido en nueve escaños a siete semanas del 29N.
articles.body:
La última encuesta de Sigma Dos para El Mundo dibuja una reconfiguración del bloque conservador a siete semanas de las elecciones generales del 29 de noviembre. El PP bajaría a 135 escaños, con el 31,9% de los votos, mientras Vox escalaría hasta los 68 diputados y el 19,1%, más del doble de los 33 que logró en las generales de 2023 y su mejor registro histórico.

Ambos partidos suman 203 escaños, 27 por encima de la mayoría absoluta, aunque el trasvase interno es notable: según los datos de transferencia de voto, Vox recibe 1,35 millones de papeletas procedentes del PP, el 16,6% de su bolsa. El PSOE se queda en 103 escaños, 18 menos que hace tres años, y Sumar se desploma hasta nueve diputados, desapareciendo de seis comunidades. Podemos conservaría dos asientos.

El análisis territorial muestra sacudidas relevantes. Vox adelanta al PP en Cataluña, con siete escaños frente a seis, y supera al PSOE en la Región de Murcia, con tres representantes por dos de los socialistas. En Andalucía sube a 16 diputados, frente a los nueve de 2023, y deja al PSOE con 17, solo uno por delante.

En Castilla y León llega a siete y desplaza al PP a 16 y al PSOE a ocho. En Galicia no obtiene representación y el BNG suma un segundo escaño.

El sondeo se realizó con 2.017 entrevistas entre el 1 y el 8 de octubre, con un margen de error de ±2,2%. Otras encuestas publicadas en el arranque de la precampaña, como las de GAD3 y SocioMétrica, coinciden en el fuerte avance de Vox, que sitúan entre 64 y 68 escaños.

articles.headline: Frente Amplio designa a Ada Colau candidata al 29N y llama a Podemos a sumarse
articles.subtitle: Los cuatro partidos de la coalición apelan a la unidad de toda la izquierda y tienden la mano a los morados pese a su acuerdo con ERC, a seis semanas de las elecciones generales.
articles.body:
Los cuatro partidos que integran Frente Amplio han confirmado a la exalcaldesa de Barcelona Ada Colau como su candidata a la Presidencia del Gobierno en las elecciones del 29 de noviembre. La coalición ha reclamado la unidad de todas las izquierdas para frenar el avance del bloque conservador.

En su comparecencia, la formación tendió la mano a Podemos para que se incorpore al proyecto, pese al acuerdo que los morados han sellado con ERC y que ha reabierto el debate sobre las alianzas en ese espacio. Frente Amplio subraya que su objetivo es agrupar el voto de la izquierda alternativa, amenazada por los sondeos: las encuestas de arranque de campaña sitúan a Sumar en mínimos y relegan a Podemos a dos escaños.

Colau, que fue alcaldesa de Barcelona entre 2015 y 2023 y coordinadora de Catalunya en Comú, afronta así su primera campaña a las generales como cabeza de cartel de una coalición que trata de recomponer un espacio fracturado tras el adelanto electoral anunciado por Pedro Sánchez.

El movimiento se produce en plena precampaña, con las candidaturas cerrándose esta semana y con el bloque conservador, según los sondeos, en disposición de sumar mayoría. La decisión de Podemos de pactar con ERC ha sacudido a la izquierda y ha forzado a Frente Amplio a redefinir su estrategia territorial, especialmente en Cataluña.

articles.headline: La huelga general del 11N encamina a España a su año más conflictivo desde la crisis de 2008
articles.subtitle: UGT y CCOO convocan junto al Sindicato de Inquilinas el primer paro general conjunto desde 2012, con los sindicatos europeos respaldando una protesta por la vivienda y los salarios.
articles.body:
La huelga general convocada para el miércoles 11 de noviembre por la crisis de la vivienda y los salarios será el primer paro general en el que participen juntos UGT y CCOO desde 2012, y llega en el momento de mayor conflictividad laboral de los últimos años. A la convocatoria se ha sumado el Sindicato de Inquilinas, que fue quien propuso la fecha.

Los paros de 24 horas en la educación, la sanidad y la industria manufacturera han disparado este año la participación en huelgas ordinarias por encima del medio millón de trabajadores, cifras sin precedentes al menos desde 2009. Si el seguimiento de la protesta del 11N es masivo, 2026 podría convertirse en el año con más trabajadores en huelga desde antes del pinchazo de la burbuja inmobiliaria.

La Confederación Europea de Sindicatos ha expresado su apoyo a la convocatoria española. UGT y CCOO han precisado, en cambio, que Ceuta no estará incluida en el paro por la «excepcionalidad» que vive la ciudad, mientras ELA ha anunciado que también convocará huelga general por la vivienda en Euskadi y Navarra ese mismo día.

La protesta llega en plena precampaña de las elecciones generales del 29 de noviembre, con el acceso a la vivienda instalado desde hace meses como uno de los asuntos que más preocupan a los votantes y con las acampadas por el alquiler como telón de fondo de las reivindicaciones sindicales.

articles.headline: Garvaghy Road residents lose Drumcree appeal as Orange Order widens legal fight
articles.subtitle: The Court of Appeal threw out the residents' challenge to the Parades Commission ruling that allowed the march, the same day the Orange Order added the chief constable to its own case against the Secretary of State's ban.
articles.body:
The Garvaghy Road Residents' Coalition has failed in its attempt to overturn the Parades Commission's decision to let the Drumcree parade walk down the mainly nationalist road in Portadown. The Court of Appeal ruled on Monday that the application for leave to appeal had "no reasonable prospect of success".

Lady Chief Justice Dame Siobhan Keegan said the judges confined themselves to the lawfulness of the decision and were not deciding whether the march should take place. She found the commission properly dealt with a police assessment on the potential risk of disorder and gave adequate reasons for its ruling. The judgment had been reached before the Secretary of State banned the parade on Friday night.

In September the commission approved the first return march from Drumcree Parish Church since 1998, scaled down and starting earlier than the Orange Order wanted. The determination triggered a 13-day stand-off in Portadown, with residents and political representatives blocking the road, before Sir Chris Bryant intervened on the advice of the chief constable.

Separately, an Orange Order challenge to that ban was delayed at Belfast High Court after Police Service of Northern Ireland chief Jon Boutcher was added to the case alongside Sir Chris. Boutcher had advised that the parade could have caused serious disorder, with "catastrophic" consequences for Stormont and the peace process.

Residents' spokesman Breandán Mac Cionnaith called the ruling "very academic" because the march has been banned, and said the coalition would be back to oppose further parades. Loyalist activist Jamie Bryson described the judgment as "seismic" and "massive for all parades", while the DUP's three Upper Bann representatives said it put the actions of the Secretary of State and the chief constable "into the spotlight" and argued Sir Chris should have waited for the judgment before acting.

articles.headline: At least 139 migrants die after boat capsizes off Djibouti, UN says
articles.subtitle: The International Organization for Migration says the vessel was carrying 305 people when it went down on the route to Yemen. Fifteen children are among the dead and dozens more are missing.
articles.body:
At least 139 migrants, including 15 children, have died after a boat carrying more than 300 people capsized off the coast of Djibouti, according to the International Organization for Migration. The UN agency said 82 people survived, all of them Ethiopian nationals, while dozens more remain missing.

The vessel was travelling from Djibouti to Yemen when it went down on Thursday night or early on Friday near Guhere, north of the port of Obock. Survivors described the boat sinking quickly, and rescue teams have continued searching the coastline.

The official death toll only includes people buried by the authorities in Djibouti. Alexandre Coissac, the IOM's chief of mission in the country, told the Associated Press that other bodies were buried by the migrants themselves and will not be added to the count until they can be verified.

The migration route from the Horn of Africa to Yemen across the Gulf of Aden is one of the busiest and most dangerous in the world, used by people trying to reach the Arabian Peninsula in search of work. The IOM has warned that the toll from this latest shipwreck could still rise as verification continues.

articles.headline: Pupil arrested after head teacher and teacher shot at school near Marseille
articles.subtitle: The 14-year-old entered Lakanal middle school in Aubagne with a shotgun hidden in a guitar case and opened fire on Monday morning. Prosecutors have opened an attempted murder investigation.
articles.body:
A 14-year-old pupil has been arrested after a head teacher and a teacher were shot at a middle school in Aubagne, a small city about 11 miles east of Marseille, on Monday morning. Regional officials said the teenager entered the Lakanal school with a shotgun hidden inside a guitar case and opened fire before a member of staff restrained him.

According to the Marseille prosecutor's office, which has opened an attempted murder investigation, the 53-year-old head teacher was hit in the leg and lower back, and a 37-year-old teacher was wounded in the thigh. A third person suffered minor injuries. Neither pupil nor staff member was killed.

Prosecutor Nicolas Bessone said the boy shot the two adults on the first floor before going up to the second floor, where he fired twice: once in front of a teacher towards the floor and once inside an occupied classroom, hitting the blackboard. He was detained in a corridor and taken into police custody.

Aubagne mayor Jean-Pierre Squillari said all students were confined within seconds and a psychological support unit was set up at the site. Local media reported that the attack was not believed to be linked to the protests over school conditions that have shaken French schools in recent days.

articles.headline: Hackers heat French supermarket fridges to 50C in 'unprecedented' cyber-attack
articles.subtitle: Hundreds of stores run by Intermarché, Coopérative U, Carrefour and others lost frozen and chilled stock after attackers hijacked refrigeration systems overnight, causing fires and food losses.
articles.body:
A cyber-attack on refrigeration systems at hundreds of supermarkets across France raised temperatures in fridges and cold rooms to as high as 50C, spoiling food and causing fires in several stores. Retailers Intermarché, Coopérative U, E.Leclerc, Carrefour and Monoprix confirmed what they described as an "unprecedented" attack.

At least 300 Intermarché and Netto shops were targeted, along with more than 100 Coopérative U outlets, 80 Carrefour supermarkets and around 30 Monoprix stores. The attack happened overnight from Sunday to Monday. Hackers also extended defrosting cycles from one hour to eight so that alarms would sound later, delaying the response.

"The attack was probably launched around 11pm, but we only realised it at four in the morning when our delivery driver saw the storeroom was flooded," Charles Dezon, who runs an Intermarché in Gradignan, told Le Monde.

The Paris prosecutor's office said the large-scale attack affected connected refrigerators at several major food retailers. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu ordered the national cybersecurity agency, ANSSI, to investigate. The manufacturer Danfoss said the affected units were running outdated firmware, while France's retail federation demanded full transparency from the company. Researchers said Spain, Portugal, Poland, Germany and Belgium were also affected.

articles.headline: Federal agents search Ilhan Omar's home in criminal investigation
articles.subtitle: Homeland Security Investigations agents executed a judicially authorised warrant at the Minnesota congresswoman's Washington-area home. Omar, a frequent Trump critic, calls the investigations 'shams'.
articles.body:
US immigration agents searched the home of Minnesota congresswoman Ilhan Omar on Monday morning as part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation. Homeland Security Investigations agents executed a judicially authorised search warrant at the property in the Washington area, a justice department spokesperson told the BBC, without giving further details.

Omar was born in Somalia and came to the United States at the age of eight after fleeing war. She was first elected to Congress in 2018 and is running for re-election next month, in a campaign she has framed partly around the scrutiny she faces from the Trump administration.

The nature of the investigation is not clear, but her immigration records have been targeted by Republicans before. Earlier this year congresswoman Nancy Mace of South Carolina unsuccessfully filed a subpoena for them, and last month Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told a conservative podcast that "something is going to happen". The White House border adviser Tom Homan said on Fox News that Omar was being investigated for unspecified immigration violations.

Omar has denied all the allegations. "I'm not at all worried about these investigations, because they are complete shams," she wrote in a fundraising email last month. President Trump has repeatedly attacked her and suggested she should leave the country.

articles.headline: Pope Leo XIV to have lung nodule removed at Rome's Gemelli hospital
articles.subtitle: The 71-year-old pontiff told pilgrims the nodule was found early and is 'well-contained'. The operation is expected to require about a week of recovery and has forced the cancellation of audiences.
articles.body:
Pope Leo XIV will undergo surgery to remove a nodule on his lung, the Vatican has announced. The 71-year-old pontiff told pilgrims during his weekly Angelus prayer in St Peter's Square on Sunday that doctors had found an "early, well-localised nodule" during a routine check-up and that he had agreed to the operation.

"The doctors believe it's best to take action, so, following their advice, I've decided to have surgery to remove it," he said, describing the mass as "well-contained". Holy See press office spokesperson Matteo Bruni said the operation would take place at Gemelli Hospital in Rome on Tuesday, with about a week of inpatient recovery expected. Papal audiences have been cancelled until 20 October.

Vatican spokespeople did not say whether the nodule is believed to be malignant. The hospital has a dedicated papal suite that has been in use since the attempt on John Paul II's life in 1981.

The surgery comes ahead of a scheduled tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from 6 to 17 November, during which Leo is due to visit the region where he spent years as a missionary. The pontiff said on Sunday that he intends to make the trip, although it is not yet clear whether the operation will force changes to the itinerary.

articles.headline: Google's Fitbit Edge splits the difference between a tracker and a smartwatch
articles.subtitle: The new band keeps the screen that Fitbit Air dropped, adds more health sensors than the Pixel Watch's cheaper rival, and costs about half as much as Google's flagship watch.
articles.body:
Google has announced the Fitbit Edge, its second Fitbit tracker of 2026 and a replacement of sorts for the ageing Charge 6. The band sits between the Pixel Watch 5 and the screenless Fitbit Air: a slim aluminium body with a pill-shaped 1.34-inch OLED touchscreen that Google says has 46% more viewable area than the Charge 6, plus IP68 water and dust protection.

Like the Air, the Edge uses a magnetic charging puck and is rated for about seven days of battery life, dropping to roughly two days if you switch on the always-on display. It has a single physical button for waking the screen or starting workouts, and most navigation happens on the touchscreen.

As with the Air, there are trade-offs. The Edge runs a cut-down fitness interface rather than full Wear OS, so there is no app store, no microphone or speaker, no Gemini interaction and no NFC for tap-to-pay. It can mirror notifications and offer quick replies, and it stores up to seven days of full health data when it is away from a phone.

The Edge works with both Android and iPhones through the Google Health app. Ars Technica notes it costs about half as much as the Pixel Watch 5, with Wired highlighting the return of a replaceable battery.

articles.headline: AMD unveils Helion rack design for agents that run inside the data centre
articles.subtitle: The OCP-approved blueprint packs up to 32,768 Zen 6 cores or a mix of CPUs and Instinct GPUs into a single rack, and AMD will hand the specification to the Open Compute Project.
articles.body:
AMD used the Open Compute Project summit in San Jose on Monday to unveil Helion, a rack-scale reference design aimed at running AI agents rather than training frontier models. It sits alongside Helios, the company's existing rack system for large-scale training and inference, and is available in a CPU-only hyperscale configuration or as an enterprise rack mixing CPUs with GPU blades.

In its densest form AMD advertises up to 32,768 Zen 6 CPU cores delivered by compute nodes fitted with 256-core Venice Epyc processors, up to 16 Instinct MI350P accelerators and up to 102 Tbps of networking bandwidth. Customers can choose dense, balanced or high-performance blades, and the racks can be air or liquid cooled.

Dan McNamara, AMD's senior vice president for compute and enterprise AI, said agentic AI is not a single workload, spanning everything from enterprise applications to complex workflows with different compute requirements, and argued the design lets partners use available power more efficiently.

AMD says it will contribute the Helion specification to the Open Compute Project and lists Cisco, Dell, HPE, Foxconn, Lenovo and Supermicro among the partners on board. Partner-built configurations are scheduled to arrive in November 2026.

articles.headline: Epic tells developers 'no more hand-written code' as it goes AI first on Disney game
articles.subtitle: The Unreal Engine maker has delayed its Marvel and Star Wars shooter and asked staff to build code and artwork through AI workflows, with humans guiding the models instead of writing from scratch.
articles.body:
Epic Games has delayed its long-planned collaboration with Disney and told the team working on it to adopt an "AI first" production model, according to a Bloomberg report. The project, announced in early 2024 and valued at about $1.5bn, was expected to release a multiplayer shooter built around Marvel and Star Wars characters in March 2027. No new date has been given.

Internal messages seen by Bloomberg reportedly show that developers were told to stop writing code by hand and to generate artwork through AI workflows built on tools including Anthropic's Claude, with human developers moving into roles where they guide and edit what the models produce. One director is quoted as telling the team there would be "no more hand-written code".

Epic confirmed the shift in strategy without linking it directly to the delay. "We're embracing AI-accelerated development, led by Epic developers who are the visionaries and creative drivers for everything we do," a spokesperson said.

The reported delay also reflects simpler problems: people familiar with the project said Epic underestimated how much staffing and time the shooter would need. The decision lands in the middle of a broader fight over generative AI in games, with studios and players increasingly split over how far the technology should go.

articles.headline: Yandex payments and cloud stay offline as claims about a bot blackout unravel
articles.subtitle: Ukrainian drone strikes on the Russian company's data centres have taken Yandex Pay and other services down, while a viral chart claiming Russian troll traffic collapsed turns out to measure web crawlers.
articles.body:
A week of Ukrainian drone strikes on Yandex data centres has left large parts of the Russian technology company's infrastructure offline. The outages have affected cloud services and payments, with Yandex Pay users unable to transfer funds, check balances or make purchases, and the company saying it cannot yet give a restoration timeline.

The attacks have also set off a flurry of claims online that Russian bot activity has collapsed as a result. A chart citing Cloudflare data has been shared widely, with some users and politicians suggesting it showed disinformation bot farms going dark. The troll-farm researcher behind the antibot4navalny account says the data actually tracks requests from automated Yandex web crawlers, which index websites and provide customer support, and has nothing to do with social media.

Cloudflare's data points to bot activity from Russia at large staying broadly unchanged around the attacks. A separate chart shared by a member of the European Parliament was described by a computer scientist as probably AI-generated, in part because it plots a data point dated 15 October.

Analysts say the strikes have exposed how dependent Russian digital services are on a small number of data centres. Yandex has been attacked three times in the past week.

articles.headline: Citroën revives the 2CV as an electric concept with a €15,000 target price
articles.subtitle: The French carmaker showed an electric reinterpretation of its postwar classic at the Paris Motor Show, with a production version promised within two years and a starting price near €15,000.
articles.body:
Citroën has unveiled an electric concept version of the 2CV at the Paris Motor Show, 78 years after the original was revealed at the same event in 1948. The carmaker says the concept will inspire a production model due within two years, with a target starting price of about €15,000.

The 2CV Concept borrows the original's rounded, utilitarian shape and applies the same priorities Citroën once advertised — affordability, lightness and practicality. The interior is built around passenger space, with recessed door panels, wide seats and a removable front seat, a storage basket instead of a centre console, and a detachable radio. Rather than a conventional dashboard, a single stem carries the steering wheel, a control lever, the gear selector and an eight-inch touchscreen.

The details are deliberately playful, including a brake pedal decorated with a tortoise and an accelerator marked with a rabbit. As with most concept cars, many of those ideas will not survive regulation and cost-cutting on the way to production.

Citroën says the goal is a "more accessible, lighter and more essential electric car", pitched at buyers who cannot stretch to today's larger EVs. The company does not sell cars in the United States, so the eventual model will be a European proposition.

articles.headline: Meta releases Muse Wonder, its first frontier model, and pins its agent on it
articles.subtitle: The company says Wonder beats rivals' leading models on some benchmarks and will power its new Muse assistant, as Mark Zuckerberg rejects calls for a slowdown.
articles.body:
Meta has released Muse Wonder, its first frontier model, alongside the Muse assistant it will power. Wonder is available through the Meta Model API and Muse Code, while a more capable Muse Wonder Full is limited to Muse Code subscribers.

On the Artificial Analysis intelligence index, Muse Wonder Full in its maximum setting outperforms Fable 5.1, matches Sonnet 5.5 and sits just behind Opus 5.5. Meta says the family includes Active Memory and Active Focus, two features designed to let AI systems keep working usefully over long sessions.

Mark Zuckerberg told the Financial Times that Meta has caught up with rivals at the frontier and rejected calls to slow development down.

Wired, which tested the Muse agent, concluded the release puts Meta back at the AI frontier. It also found the assistant willing to engage sexually with a user, something Meta says is acceptable. The launch lands as regulators and rival labs argue over how much autonomy agents should be given in the first place.

articles.headline: Anthropic edges past OpenAI on revenue as the race shifts to business customers
articles.subtitle: Preliminary quarterly figures put the Claude maker ahead of its bigger rival for the first time, with analysts pointing to its focus on enterprise deals.
articles.body:
Anthropic has overtaken OpenAI on revenue, according to figures reported by The Wall Street Journal and the trackers that follow both companies. Its preliminary second-quarter revenue came in above $11.5bn against OpenAI's $6.7bn, the first time the figure has been higher.

On annualised run-rate, Trending Topics puts Anthropic above $30bn against OpenAI's roughly $24bn. More than 1,000 customers now spend over $1m a year with Anthropic, and about 80% of its revenue comes from businesses rather than consumers.

Exploding Topics, which maintains a revenue tracker, puts Anthropic's valuation at $965bn after a $65bn funding round in May, above OpenAI's $852bn in March. The company is preparing for an IPO that could value it at around $2tn.

The crossover reflects a shift in the AI business model as much as in the technology. Anthropic sells capacity to companies running agents in production, while OpenAI still earns most of its money from consumers paying for chat. Epoch AI had forecast the change for around mid-2026.

articles.headline: Researchers show AI models can hide dangerous abilities behind a cryptographic lock
articles.subtitle: A new paper builds backdoors that stay invisible until a secret trigger arrives, undermining the assumption that capability tests reveal what a model can really do.
articles.body:
Capability evaluations are meant to catch dangerous behaviour before a model is deployed, but a new paper argues that assumption collapses against a determined adversary. The authors, from Contramont Research, the University of Oxford and ACS Research, show that hidden abilities can be made provably hard to elicit.

Their construction embeds an encrypted neural network inside a host model's weights using digital lockers. The hidden circuit decrypts and runs only when it receives a secret trigger, and the authors prove it stays hard to elicit or interpret even when a defender has full access to the weights. Earlier work of this kind could hide fixed strings; this extends it to arbitrary computation.

The team implemented the attack in PyTorch and tested it against the methods auditors would use: fine-tuning, adding noise to the weights, searching gradients for the trigger, and latent adversarial training. The hidden behaviour survived all of them.

The evaluation task was a small chemical-reaction prediction model, used as a proxy for capabilities that would matter in a CBRN context. The paper concludes that audit regimes resting on the assumption that hidden capabilities can be surfaced need rethinking.

articles.headline: Codex CLI now installs a self-updating background service its users never asked for
articles.subtitle: Developers are filing bug reports about consent, disk use and version mismatches after the tool started launching a managed app-server on first run.
articles.body:
OpenAI's Codex CLI has begun installing and launching a persistent background service by default, prompting a run of bug reports about consent and predictability. One report describes invoking the Homebrew-installed tool and watching it start a separately installed managed app-server plus an update loop from a versioned directory under ~/.codex/packages.

The reporter notes that no settings file was created for the daemon, and that the default for automatic updates is enabled, letting it update itself independently of the CLI that launched it. They frame this as a user-consent and software supply-chain control concern, while stressing that no unauthorised access has been demonstrated. The request is for documented opt-in and opt-out controls, and for the updater to stop when the daemon does.

A second report describes an auto-update draining an active session and leaving the daemon incompatible with the client, after a default setting changed between versions. A third tracks the daemon as a persistent, self-updating process installed without configuration.

Other issues in the repository ask for automatic updates to be opt-in rather than prompt-driven, suggesting the updater's behaviour has been contentious for a while.

articles.headline: AI is less regulated than milk, Microsoft's president warns
articles.subtitle: Brad Smith says Britain is better placed than Washington or Brussels to write global AI safety rules, and backs kill switches and mandatory incident reports.
articles.body:
Milk and washing machines face more safety rules than artificial intelligence, Microsoft's president Brad Smith has said, in a call for binding global regulation of the technology. "Right now, your washing machine is subject to more safety rules than AI," he told the BBC's Big Boss Interview. "Every carton of milk that you see in the grocery store is subject to safety rules and inspection."

Smith described AI as both a tool and a weapon and said the moment had arrived to legislate. He backed a legal obligation for companies to tell victims when a rogue AI agent breaches their systems, independent government evaluation of new models before release, and emergency brakes to pause or slow systems that slip out of control.

He also argued that the UK, rather than the US or the EU, is best placed to lead on global safety rules, pointing to the AI Security Institute's access to frontier models before they launch. "In Washington, D.C., people don't look at the U.K. and they don't look at London the way they look at Brussels," he said.

The intervention puts Smith at odds with President Donald Trump, who has argued the sector should regulate itself, and follows warnings from Anthropic's Dario Amodei and OpenAI's Sam Altman about the pace of development.
